cnhl-black-1500-4s.name: CNHL Black Series 1500 4S

function.does: 4S pack. XT60 leads feed the ESC. The balance plug is a charge lead and is not an aircraft wire.

geometry.note: Size listings disagree: 75 × 35 × 37, 38 × 37 × 75, 34 × 35 × 73.5, and 37 × 35 × 75 all appear. This mesh uses 35 × 37 × 75 and lies the long axis along Z. That axis assignment is a studio choice.

price.note: DIYFPV comparison updated 2026-10-12 ran from $16.50 at Fly High FPV to $27.90. $16.50 is used. Confirm the SKU is 1501004BK. This is not the G+Plus 1501004G (191 g, 33 × 35 × 85, XT60U, listed at $16.99 at Pilots HQ).

notes: Mass 183 g includes the wire and the connector.
100C continuous on 1.5 Ah is 150 A. Four motors at the 36 A catalog peak sum to 144 A.
The balance lead is not in the flight harness.

emax-eco-ii-2306-1700.name: EMAX ECO II 2306 1700KV

function.does: 2306 class brushless motor. Three phase leads. Prop sits on the shaft adapter.

geometry.note: Body is about 28 mm across. Length is listed as 31.6 mm and also 31.5 mm. The mesh uses 31.6. The shaft mesh uses the 5 mm prop hole, not the 4 mm internal bearing. Origin is the center of the mount face. The shaft runs along +Y.

price.note: Wind Catcher $15.99 each. The page date is 2022-01-14, so this listing is old. Read it again before you order.

notes: Mass 30.4 g does not include the silicone leads.
A figure of about 1850 g on 6S was published without a prop name. It is not entered as a thrust point.
Mount pattern on this motor is 16 × 16 only. The frame also accepts 19 × 19, which this motor does not use.

gemfan-51466-v2.name: Gemfan Hurricane 51466 V2

function.does: Three-blade 5 inch polycarbonate prop. Sits on the motor shaft.

geometry.note: Disk 131.8 mm and hub thickness 6.8 mm are published. Hub diameter and blade width were not, so the viewer defaults draw those. Pitch is stored on the part and is not an airfoil.

drawing.note: The outline is the mesh bounds, which are wider than the round disk.

price.note: KiwiQuads $3.99 sale from $5.49, page dated 2025-07-24, sold as a 4-pack. covers is 4, so four props are one line.

notes: Demon Power lists the same family at 4.05 g and 129.5 mm. This file uses 4.2 g and 131.8 mm.

print-x-226.name: Printed X 226

function.does: Same square-X layout as the Source One file, for a printed stand-in. Swap this id for the carbon frame and the mounts stay put.

geometry.note: Same estimated plate and arm width as the carbon frame. Mass is the mesh volume times 1.27 g/cm³, a typical PETG density. The arm boxes overlap the plate, so the grams run high and are marked estimated. There is no published mass and no price.

drawing.note: Generated from the mesh. Edit the shared layout, not a second wheelbase.

pattern.motor_y_note: 2.5 mm bottom plate plus 6 mm arm. Both thicknesses are published. Using their sum as the motor face height is the studio datum.
pattern.stack_y_note: Bottom plate is 2.5 mm. The stack is assumed to sit on that plate.

extras.note: Y is the 2.5 mm bottom plate plus the published 30 mm standoff. The pack is centered. That sum is the studio datum, not a measured pad.
Offset to the right so the receiver clears the flight controller. Not a published coordinate.
Nose-ward of the stack. Not a published coordinate. The camera body grows toward -Z.
Aft of the stack and low, so the video transmitter clears the flight controller. Not a published coordinate. The frame does publish a 20 × 20 pattern. This port is where the studio seats the VTX.

layout.note: Change wheelbase_mm and the motor ports, arm mesh, wire spans, prop gap, and CG all move. The Source One is sold as a wide-stance X. The pages checked do not give the arm angle, so this file uses a square X at the published 226 mm diagonal and says so. Channel order is Betaflight Quad X. Nose is -Z, right is +X, up is +Y. Front-right is +X and -Z.

notes: Not a store part. Conception skips it because it has no price. The printed-yard assembly names it by hand.

radiomaster-rp1.name: RadioMaster RP1

function.does: ExpressLRS receiver. CRSF to the flight controller UART2. Pads are 5V, TX, RX, and GND.

geometry.note: Published board is 13 × 11 × 3 mm. Y is the 3 mm thickness.

price.note: HobbyTown $21.99 in stock, part RM-HP0157.RX-RP1-V2. Rotorxpress on 2025-08-23 showed $12.59 sale and $20.99 regular. The HobbyTown price is used. A Robu.in spec block for this name was discarded.

notes: 2.2 g includes the antenna. Board is 13 × 11 × 3 mm.
Firmware strings disagree across pages (v3.0 and v2.4). The repeated hardware spec is what this file keeps.
Current draw was not on the pages checked, so it is left off specs and out of the 5 V sum.

runcam-phoenix-2-micro.name: RunCam Phoenix 2 Micro

function.does: Analog micro camera. Video goes to the flight controller CAM pad. Power is the FC 5 V rail.

geometry.note: Body used here is 19 × 19 × 20 mm. The official shop SKU PHOENIX2-SL lists 19 × 19 × 19. The mesh grows toward the nose from the back face.

price.note: RaceDayQuads $35.99, SKU RUNC-PHOENIX2-SL, with 19 × 19 × 20 mm and 9 g. The official shop lists SKU PHOENIX2-SL at 19 × 19 × 19 mm and US$29.99. Depth and price both disagree. This file uses the RDQ depth, mass, and price.

notes: 200 mA at 5 V is the figure in the 5 V budget. 85 mA at 12 V is recorded and not used, because this build feeds the camera from the FC 5 V rail.
Micro silver.

speedybee-bls-55a.name: SpeedyBee BLS 55A

function.does: 4-in-1 BLHeli_S ESC. Battery leads land here. The flight controller takes power and signals through the 8-pin cable.

geometry.note: Board 45.6 × 44 × 8 mm. The mesh grows up from the mount face.

drawing.note: Phase groups are estimated corners, not a silkscreen copy.

ports.note: Rear-right phase group. Not a copied silkscreen.
Front-right phase group. Not a copied silkscreen.
Rear-left phase group. Not a copied silkscreen.
Front-left phase group. Not a copied silkscreen.

price.note: Progressive RC in stock at $39.99. DIYFPV comparison updated 2026-10-10. GetFPV listed $54.99 and was out of stock. SKU SB-BLS-55A.

notes: Burst is 70 A for 10 s on the SpeedyBee listing. HobbyRC says 50 A burst on 6S. Both are recorded. The check uses the 55 A continuous figure.
A 1000 µF low-ESR capacitor ships with the ESC and is not a separate BOM line.
Telemetry is not supported. The TEL pad is still on the 8-pin map.
The flight controller is not powered from a second pack lead. Pack positive and ground stop on this board.

speedybee-f405-v4.name: SpeedyBee F405 V4

function.does: Flight controller. Motor signals leave on the 8-pin cable. Receiver is CRSF on UART2. Camera video uses the CAM pad. The 9 V rail is not used by the TX800.

geometry.note: Published board is 41.6 × 39.4 × 7.8 mm. Y is the 7.8 mm thickness. Mount holes are 30.5 × 30.5, 4 mm.

drawing.note: Pads are electrical, not a copied silkscreen.

price.note: RaceDayQuads $45.99, SKU 21253, sold out as seen 2026-10-12. ProgressiveRC showed $39.99 unavailable and a body line saying $36.99. Those two are not used. Oscar Liang on 2024-04-13 listed the V4 stack at $69.99. That stack price is not a BOM line. Lumenier includes the 8-pin cable with the FC, so the cable is its own included part at $0.

notes: Betaflight wiki: BLE on UART4 at MSP 115200, and no user Wi-Fi. Some store pages claim Wi-Fi. The wiki is what this file follows.
UART2 is the wiki default for the receiver.
There is a CAM pad. There is no VIDEO pad aimed at the VTX. The optional vtx-video link stays open on purpose.
The 9 V 3 A rail is real. The TX800 input is 3.7–5.5 V, so no wire is drawn to 9 V.

speedybee-fc-esc-8pin.name: SpeedyBee FC-ESC 8-pin

function.does: 30 mm SH1.0 cable between the F405 V4 and the BLS 55A. Motor-signal order crosses on this cable. It is not a second geometric link.

geometry.note: The harness is the wires. This marker only gives the part a body. Mass was not published and is omitted.

drawing.note: All eight conductors share the connector point. Any fan on the sheet is presentation.

price.note: Included with the flight controller. $0 so it is not bought again. Not a separate SKU.

notes: Map follows the Betaflight wiki 8-pin table, either end: pin1 GND/N/A, pin2 BAT/CURRENT, pin3 M1/S4, pin4 M2/S3, pin5 M3/S2, pin6 M4/S1, pin7 CUR/VBAT, pin8 TEL/GND.
Length 30 mm.

speedybee-tx800.name: SpeedyBee TX800

function.does: 5.8 GHz analog video transmitter. Power is 5 V, not the flight controller 9 V rail. Video in has no matching FC pad in this build.

geometry.note: PCB is 28 × 28 mm with a 20 × 20 mount. Height of about 6 mm is only from greenchip.com.ua and is estimated. Hole diameter is not set: pages disagree between M2 and M3.

drawing.note: Generated from the mesh. The antenna is not in the body.

price.note: FPV Builds RC $34.99. DIYFPV on 2026-10-12 ranged $36.43–$65.97. ProgressiveRC $44.99 sold out, SKU AC-STX800. $34.99 is used.

notes: Mass 5.6 g is the heatsink without the antenna. Bare is also listed at 3.2 g, and 6.9 g with the antenna. The antenna is not in this mesh.
PIT mode is the 0 mW step. Power steps are PIT / 25 / 200 / 400 / 800 mW.
Current is published as 250–750 mA at 5 V. The 5 V budget uses 0.75 A so the check is the high end. 0.75 A plus the camera 0.20 A is under the 3 A BEC.
IRC Tramp is the protocol note. It is not a pad.
Do not move this part onto the 9 V rail. The input range stops at 5.5 V.

tbs-source-one-v5.name: TBS Source One V5

function.does: Carbon X quad frame. Carries the motors, the stack, the pack, the receiver, the camera, and the video transmitter.

geometry.note: Arm thickness 6 mm and bottom plate 2.5 mm are published. The 52 mm plate outline and the 12 mm arm width are not. Both are estimates so the mesh has a body. Mass stays the published 123.5 g, not this volume. V5 and V5.1 share the numbers used here. The V5.1 Gorilla mount is not modeled. The hardware kit stays inside this part.

drawing.note: The studio sheet is drawn from the mesh. This block is the title note. A wheelbase edit moves the sheet.

pattern.motor_y_note: 2.5 mm bottom plate plus 6 mm arm. Both thicknesses are published. Using their sum as the motor face height is the studio datum.
pattern.stack_y_note: Bottom plate is 2.5 mm. The stack is assumed to sit on that plate.

extras.note: Y is the 2.5 mm bottom plate plus the published 30 mm standoff. The pack is centered. That sum is the studio datum, not a measured pad.
Offset to the right so the receiver clears the flight controller. Not a published coordinate.
Nose-ward of the stack. Not a published coordinate. The camera body grows toward -Z.
Aft of the stack and low, so the video transmitter clears the flight controller. Not a published coordinate. The frame does publish a 20 × 20 pattern. This port is where the studio seats the VTX.

layout.note: Change wheelbase_mm and the motor ports, arm mesh, wire spans, prop gap, and CG all move. The Source One is sold as a wide-stance X. The pages checked do not give the arm angle, so this file uses a square X at the published 226 mm diagonal and says so. Channel order is Betaflight Quad X. Nose is -Z, right is +X, up is +Y. Front-right is +X and -Z.

price.note: Rotorxpress page dated 2025-08-23 showed $22.79 sale and $37.99 regular. The regular price is used. Tytoview listed €43 and was sold out. Confirm before ordering.

notes: Wide-stance X is what the pages call it. The arm angle was not published, so the shared layout uses a square X on the 226 mm diagonal.
Camera accepts 19 mm or 20 mm micro. Motor pattern is 16 × 16 and 19 × 19. Props up to 5.2 in. The low end of prop_in is not a published minimum.

camera-micro-19.name: 19 mm micro camera
camera-micro-19.note: Size class for a 19 mm micro camera body. A hole pattern was not used, because the Phoenix 2 pages checked describe the body, not a bolt circle.

motor-mount-16x16.name: 16 × 16 mm motor
motor-mount-16x16.note: 16 mm center to center is the pattern. The ECO II pages checked did not include a hole drawing, so the bolt size is left blank.

motor-mount-19x19.name: 19 × 19 mm motor
motor-mount-19x19.note: 19 mm center to center is the pattern. Bolt size is left blank until a drawing names it. A motor that only lists this pattern will not mate to a frame that only lists 16 × 16.

prop-shaft-m5.name: 5 mm prop shaft
prop-shaft-m5.note: The 51466 V2 hole is 5 mm. The ECO II bearing shaft is 4 mm inside the motor. The prop seats on the adapter, not on that bearing.

stack-20.name: 20 × 20 mm stack
stack-20.note: 20 mm center to center is the published TX800 mount and the Source One 20 × 20 stack. TX800 hole callouts disagree (M2 on some pages, M3 on others). No hole diameter is chosen here.

stack-30.5.name: 30.5 × 30.5 mm stack
stack-30.5.note: Spacing is the published 30.5 mm stack. The BLS 55A listing says 4 mm holes. The Source One frame hole diameter was not stated. Oscar Liang notes M3 bolts because of the grommets. The bolt field stays empty so those two facts are not collapsed into one invented hole.

strap.name: Strap or pad
strap.note: A soft mount. Battery and receiver use it. There is no bolt circle to get wrong.

eco-1700-51466-4s.name: ECO II 1700KV + Hurricane 51466 V2 on 4S
eco-1700-51466-4s.note: No static thrust table for this motor, this prop, and 4S was on the pages checked. Leave points empty until a real table is pasted. Each point is { throttle, thrust_g, current_a }. Thrust-to-weight and hover minutes stay blank until then. Do not invent grams.

wire.note: copper_ohm_m is the usual resistivity of annealed copper near 20 °C. It is a standard constant, not a measurement from these parts. slack multiplies the straight-line span. Factory lead length stays on the part as specs.lead_mm and is not overwritten. awg.mm2 values are the standard conductor areas for those gauges.

flight.note: prop_gap_mm is the minimum clearance between adjacent prop disks. cg_mm is the horizontal distance from the hub that raises a warning. drop_frac is judged against cells times 3.7 V, the nominal pack voltage, not a full charge. usable is the share of capacity counted toward hover minutes. pack_punch scales the sum of catalog motor peaks before that sum is compared with the pack continuous current. 1 leaves the catalog peaks unscaled.
